context: The prompt requests removing the Prompts History tab from the Web UI since all prompt information is now available in the Workdir section through the registry view. The Prompts History page currently displays completed prompts in a table format with view/edit buttons and supports filtering. The goal is to simplify the interface by eliminating redundancy while ensuring no functionality is lost.

questions.question-text: Should the prompt viewing functionality currently provided by Prompts History be preserved elsewhere?

options.label: Yes, migrate the view/edit modal functionality to the Workdir page so clicking prompts in the registry opens them
options.pros: Preserves existing functionality, users can still view/edit completed prompts, seamless transition from Prompts History to Workdir
options.cons: Requires additional implementation in Workdir page, increases complexity of registry view

options.label: No, remove the viewing functionality entirely since prompt files can be accessed directly in the file system
options.pros: Simplest implementation, encourages direct file access, reduces Web UI maintenance
options.cons: Loss of convenient UI-based viewing, users must navigate file system manually, degraded user experience

options.label: Partial - only preserve read-only viewing, remove edit functionality
options.pros: Simpler than full migration, provides reference capability without editing risks, focuses Workdir on information display
options.cons: Loses edit capability which may be useful for corrections, inconsistent with current Workdir design

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A maintains feature parity while consolidating the interface. Since the Workdir registry already provides navigation via clickable prompt titles (based on P-050 implementation), extending this to open a view/edit modal is consistent and preserves the convenient UI-based workflow users expect.

user-selection.value: It is already migrated. Check it.

questions.question-text: What should happen to the backend API endpoint /api/prompts-list that serves the Prompts History page?

options.label: Remove it completely since it will no longer be used
options.pros: Clean removal of unused code, reduces API surface area, simpler codebase
options.cons: May be referenced elsewhere, could break if any other code depends on it

options.label: Keep it but deprecate it for potential future use or CLI access
options.pros: Maintains backward compatibility, provides programmatic access to prompts list, useful for scripting
options.cons: Maintains unused code in production, adds maintenance burden, could confuse future developers

options.label: Check for dependencies first, then decide based on usage
options.pros: Safe approach, ensures nothing breaks, informed decision based on actual usage
options.cons: Requires additional analysis time, may delay the removal

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C is the safest approach. Before removing any API endpoint, we should verify it's not used by other parts of the system (CLI tools, automation scripts, etc.). If no dependencies exist, proceed with removal (Option A). This prevents unexpected breakage.

user-selection.value: Depends if the endpoints are used in Workdir page or other pages.

questions.question-text: How should the loadPromptsHistory() JavaScript function and related UI code be handled?

options.label: Remove all Prompts History related JavaScript functions, HTML elements, and CSS entirely
options.pros: Complete cleanup, reduces code size, eliminates maintenance of unused code, clearer codebase
options.cons: Requires careful identification of all related code, risk of breaking if something is missed

options.label: Comment out the code initially, verify everything works, then remove in a later step
options.pros: Safer incremental approach, easy to rollback if issues arise, allows testing without permanent deletion
options.cons: Leaves commented code in repository temporarily, adds extra cleanup step, not a final solution

options.label: Refactor some reusable functions (like viewCompletedPrompt modal) to be shared with Workdir, remove Prompts History specific code
options.pros: Preserves useful functionality, promotes code reuse, cleaner architecture with shared utilities
options.cons: More complex refactoring, requires careful separation of concerns, takes more implementation time

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C aligns with good software engineering practices. If Q1 answer is A (preserve viewing functionality), we'll need the modal code anyway. Refactoring it into shared utility functions makes the codebase more maintainable and enables reuse across different sections.

user-selection.value: Depends if it is used in other pages

questions.question-text: Should the navigation menu item for Prompts History be removed completely or replaced?

options.label: Remove the menu item entirely and reduce the number of tabs
options.pros: Cleaner navigation bar, fewer options for users to choose from, focuses attention on remaining sections
options.cons: May disorient users who are accustomed to the current layout, sudden change in navigation

options.label: Replace it with a different useful section (e.g., Files & Folders structure view)
options.pros: Maintains consistent number of navigation items, no gap in menu, introduces potentially useful feature
options.cons: Requires implementing new functionality, may not be needed now, adds scope to this task

options.label: Remove the menu item but keep the same overall navigation structure
options.pros: Simple direct removal, preserves current navigation patterns for other sections, minimal changes
options.cons: Creates asymmetry in navigation bar, may look incomplete with odd number of items

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A is the cleanest approach consistent with the goal of removing redundancy. Since Workdir now provides all prompt information via the registry view, there's no need to preserve the menu item or replace it. Users will adapt to the simplified navigation quickly.

questions.question-text: Are there any references or links to Prompts History from other parts of the application that need to be addressed?

options.label: Yes, search comprehensively for all references (HTML comments, documentation, code comments, etc.) and update/remove them
options.pros: Thorough cleanup, prevents broken links or references, maintains documentation accuracy, professional result
options.cons: Time-consuming, requires careful search across all files, may find many references to update

options.label: Only update critical code references, leave documentation and comments for later
options.pros: Faster implementation, focuses on functional aspects first, documentation can be updated incrementally
options.cons: Leaves outdated documentation, may confuse future developers, incomplete cleanup

options.label: Update code references and add a migration note in relevant documentation explaining the change
options.pros: Balances thoroughness with efficiency, provides context for the change, helps users understand what happened
options.cons: Still requires documentation updates, migration notes may become outdated over time

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A ensures complete and professional removal. Since this is a deliberate architectural change to simplify the interface, all references should be updated to reflect the new structure. This prevents confusion and maintains the quality of the codebase and documentation.
